The long crossing begins at the lower-left of Soit, rises through the word, and continues with a shallow rise across en effet through both tall f strokes and the terminal t. The phrase Soit en effet is legible under that single cancellation. Si on a is legible on the next baseline; its a has a small white counter and joined dark lower shape. No new lexical doubt is added there.

The selected addition against C and H is the explicitly preserved long sloping cancellation geometry. Count C1/H1, high confidence, kind drawing or diagram; marked_in_H false. root_count_authorization.literal:
## 03 — overwritten relation and following E/index

Crop: `readers/025/C/03_intersection.png`, full box [1000,90,1390,240], successfully viewed once after an earlier failed unseen delivery.

Two short nearly horizontal runs extend from the left into a heavy arch. The upper run crosses the arch near its shoulder; the lower run lies beneath it and has a short left spur. The arch rises from a left-sloping entry and falls to a heavy right stem. Those surviving transverse strokes support the old-equals reading, while their crossings also leave the predecessor/retrace allocation open. Select complete `C025-G02`, with all three source candidates in order: deleted equals followed by cap; cap with unidentified crossed predecessor; cap with two transverse retraces. The literal two runs and arch remain present in every candidate. Original C025-R02-1 remains retained, low confidence; its mere retention is C0. The explicit surviving geometry and whole relation qualification carry one physical C1/H1, medium confidence, kind drawing or diagram.

The following E has an upright that bends into the bottom arm, a separate middle arm and a shallow upper curve visibly detached at the left. One small high point accompanies a lower short bent index stroke that turns left at its foot. The point and bend leave i/j unresolved; i remains the primary reading. The detached upper curve's top-arm versus independent-run role also remains open. Select complete `C025-E01`, preserving E_i/top arm, E_j/top arm, E_i/independent upper curve, E_j/independent upper curve in that order. Keep the single observed high point inside this complete qualified index group; add no extra point. His hand applies to the main E/index; undetermined hand is retained for the independent-upper-curve candidate only. Original C025-R03-1 remains retained, low confidence, C0 for retention itself. Added head-role qualification and full geometry share one physical C1/H1, medium confidence, kind drawing or diagram.

Reader B owns the relation and E/index in one complete group B025-G02; retain that complete four-state own proposal in the record without splitting it into invented B candidates. A's own old-equals decision and E j/i order, and C's full two groups, remain as sourced. The ordinary barred U, nonempty sign, empty-set slash and comma remain outside the two selected groups. marked_in_H is false for both physical loci; there is no local H doubt apparatus here.

## 04 — cancelled et si and live alors

Crop: `readers/025/A/crops/03_crossed_et_si.png`, full box [1390, 125, 1668, 225], successfully viewed once.

The e loop leads to the tall t; the following s has an open curved head above the crossing, and the i retains one high dot. A long descending cancellation crosses both words, from the e/t level at the left through the lower si body to its far-right endpoint. The live alors follows after a gap, with a closed initial a and tall l. Select complete C025-G03 for deleted et si and the observed descending cancellation; keep ordinary live alors outside. A supplies its own literal cancellation group and B the ordinary deleted et si text. The phrase itself agrees with C and differs from H's deleted ainsi; the explicit sloping path adds the geometry to both witnesses. Count one physical C1/H1, high confidence, kind drawing or diagram, his hand, marked_in_H false. No new doubt or original C doubt is assigned here.

## 06 — main union, high cross, hat and upper-index traces

Crop: `readers/025/A/crops/05_union_hat_sigma.png`, full box [805, 240, 1080, 410], successfully viewed once.

The large operator has doubled left and right stems and a heavily retraced rounded bowl. A nearly horizontal dark stroke crosses high on the left stem and extends rightward; above it, a thinner arch enters from the left and curves into that stem. Select the complete C025-G05 literal operator, retaining both complete source candidates: high-cross union, and deleted earlier intersection with live union. The high cross is firm; the allocation of the thinner upper arch and doubled strokes to an earlier state remains unresolved. Keep the lower alpha-in-K limit once, outside the operator group. Original C025-R04-1 is retained, medium confidence, with C0 for retention itself. Literal geometry gives one physical C1/H1, medium confidence, kind drawing or diagram. H's note describing a disjoint-union sign supplies no uncertainty macro or alternate ink reading; marked_in_H false. No meaning of the high cross is proved or substituted here.

The hatted Sigma has a pale joined head/body entry, a curved diagonal turn, a long lower foot and a separate clear two-stroke plus. The hat rises to a blunt peak and descends to a short right tail. The alpha has an oval left loop, a rising right stroke and a crossing lower branch. Two tiny traces sit above it: a dark angular point and, above-left of that point, a much fainter short slash. Select complete A025-S02, including its nested A025-M01 exactly once; preserve both separate alpha paths. The main hatted Sigma, alpha and plus remain firm, his hand. The two traces remain locally qualified with hand, role, attachment and surface origin undetermined; their presence does not settle their allocation to the index. A's local nested qualification, B's complete own qualified state and C's complete two candidates remain fully distinct in the record. Count one physical C1/H1 for the complete literal glyph with its added two-trace scope, medium confidence; the two-trace allocation itself is low confidence. Kind drawing or diagram, marked_in_H false. No original C doubt belongs to this hatted-glyph locus.

root_count_authorization.literal:
## 06 — main union, high cross, hat and upper-index traces

Crop: `readers/025/A/crops/05_union_hat_sigma.png`, full box [805, 240, 1080, 410], successfully viewed once.

The large operator has doubled left and right stems and a heavily retraced rounded bowl. A nearly horizontal dark stroke crosses high on the left stem and extends rightward; above it, a thinner arch enters from the left and curves into that stem. Select the complete C025-G05 literal operator, retaining both complete source candidates: high-cross union, and deleted earlier intersection with live union. The high cross is firm; the allocation of the thinner upper arch and doubled strokes to an earlier state remains unresolved. Keep the lower alpha-in-K limit once, outside the operator group. Original C025-R04-1 is retained, medium confidence, with C0 for retention itself. Literal geometry gives one physical C1/H1, medium confidence, kind drawing or diagram. H's note describing a disjoint-union sign supplies no uncertainty macro or alternate ink reading; marked_in_H false. No meaning of the high cross is proved or substituted here.

The hatted Sigma has a pale joined head/body entry, a curved diagonal turn, a long lower foot and a separate clear two-stroke plus. The hat rises to a blunt peak and descends to a short right tail. The alpha has an oval left loop, a rising right stroke and a crossing lower branch. Two tiny traces sit above it: a dark angular point and, above-left of that point, a much fainter short slash. Select complete A025-S02, including its nested A025-M01 exactly once; preserve both separate alpha paths. The main hatted Sigma, alpha and plus remain firm, his hand. The two traces remain locally qualified with hand, role, attachment and surface origin undetermined; their presence does not settle their allocation to the index. A's local nested qualification, B's complete own qualified state and C's complete two candidates remain fully distinct in the record. Count one physical C1/H1 for the complete literal glyph with its added two-trace scope, medium confidence; the two-trace allocation itself is low confidence. Kind drawing or diagram, marked_in_H false. No original C doubt belongs to this hatted-glyph locus.

## 08 — condition Sigma, E_alpha and crossed endpoint

Crop: `readers/025/A/crops/07_pi_edge_deletion.png`, full box [1208, 333, 1670, 425], successfully viewed once.

Its alpha is a short loop with a rising right branch and low tail; the plus is a distinct short cross. Select complete C025-S03, firm, his hand. Preserve the following membership, pi with its small closed zero, opening parenthesis, X and set-minus stroke as ordinary companions. root_count_authorization.literal:
## 08 — condition Sigma, E_alpha and crossed endpoint

Crop: `readers/025/A/crops/07_pi_edge_deletion.png`, full box [1208, 333, 1670, 425], successfully viewed once.

The condition Sigma has a thin continuous contact from its upper horizontal into the descending diagonal, a sharp middle turn, and a long low foot. Its alpha is a short loop with a rising right branch and low tail; the plus is a distinct short cross. Select complete C025-S03, firm, his hand. Preserve the following membership, pi with its small closed zero, opening parenthesis, X and set-minus stroke as ordinary companions. Count C1/H1 for the complete literal Sigma geometry, high confidence, kind drawing or diagram, marked_in_H false.

The E inside the pi-zero argument has a detached top horizontal, an upright bending into the lower arm, a separate middle arm, and a clear alpha. Select the exact C025-E02 path group, adding one outer unsure wrapper locally around that complete group. Retain the two full states E_alpha with detached top arm and E_alpha with independent upper run; the upper-run role stays qualified at this occurrence. His hand applies to the E/alpha body; undetermined hand applies only to the independent-upper-run candidate. A and B keep their own firm E proposals. The wrapper is the sole root change to the selected C source group; preserve every path and coordinate. Count C1/H1, medium confidence, kind drawing or diagram, marked_in_H false.

At the far right, a tall upright, a sharply rising crossing diagonal, a folded middle loop, a short curved right upright and a long low rightward crossing run survive together. The crossings leave the complete letter sequence unresolved. Select complete C025-G07 with deleted les, deleted K and deleted tel in its source order, retaining all five paths. Original C025-R05-1 remains retained, low confidence; the original les/K retention itself is C0. The added complete tel alternative and literal geometry form one physical C1/H1, low confidence, kind drawing or diagram. The visible terminal run supplies no separate comma; none is added. This same cluster includes the H comma difference, without another count. His hand; marked_in_H false.

## 09 — pre-les cluster and Sigma foot touching alpha

Crop: `readers/025/A/crops/08_crossed_U_Sigma.png`, full box [1070, 420, 1380, 525], successfully viewed once.

The cluster before les has a broad U-like lower bowl, a tall right stem, a diagonal triangular crossing through its upper-right area and a short low return hook. Their intersections do not isolate a separate cancellation stroke. Select complete C025-G08 with all five full candidates in source order: deleted U-Sigma, deleted union-Sigma, deleted U, live U-Sigma, live et. Retain the three original cancelled C candidates under C025-R06-1, which stays retained, low confidence. Keep A's and B's four-state own proposals without adding C's live-et candidate to them. The extra live-state possibilities and the full surviving geometry carry one physical C1/H1, low confidence, kind drawing or diagram; the original three-way retention itself is C0. His hand; marked_in_H false. Live les stays outside this group.

The next Sigma has a short heavy detached upper run, a separate lower descending entry, a sharp middle turn and a low foot that touches the alpha at its right end. The alpha rises into a short curl and returns through a small lower loop to a rightward tail. The plus is a separate dark cross. Select the exact C025-S04 complete group, including its single shared body-foot/alpha path, and add one outer unsure wrapper locally. Retain both full states: Sigma_alpha^+ with detached head/retrace, and Sigma_alpha^+ with independent upper run. The body and attached alpha remain his hand; the independent-upper-run candidate retains undetermined hand for that run. The wrapper is the sole root change to this C group; preserve all coordinates and paths. A's own two touching paths and B's own font-index proposal stay complete in their source states. Count one physical C1/H1, medium confidence, kind drawing or diagram, marked_in_H false.

## 09 — pre-les cluster and Sigma foot touching alpha

Crop: `readers/025/A/crops/08_crossed_U_Sigma.png`, full box [1070, 420, 1380, 525], successfully viewed once.

The cluster before les has a broad U-like lower bowl, a tall right stem, a diagonal triangular crossing through its upper-right area and a short low return hook. Their intersections do not isolate a separate cancellation stroke. Select complete C025-G08 with all five full candidates in source order: deleted U-Sigma, deleted union-Sigma, deleted U, live U-Sigma, live et. Retain the three original cancelled C candidates under C025-R06-1, which stays retained, low confidence. Keep A's and B's four-state own proposals without adding C's live-et candidate to them. The extra live-state possibilities and the full surviving geometry carry one physical C1/H1, low confidence, kind drawing or diagram; the original three-way retention itself is C0. His hand; marked_in_H false. Live les stays outside this group.

The next Sigma has a short heavy detached upper run, a separate lower descending entry, a sharp middle turn and a low foot that touches the alpha at its right end. The alpha rises into a short curl and returns through a small lower loop to a rightward tail. The plus is a separate dark cross. Select the exact C025-S04 complete group, including its single shared body-foot/alpha path, and add one outer unsure wrapper locally. Retain both full states: Sigma_alpha^+ with detached head/retrace, and Sigma_alpha^+ with independent upper run. The body and attached alpha remain his hand; the independent-upper-run candidate retains undetermined hand for that run. The wrapper is the sole root change to this C group; preserve all coordinates and paths. A's own two touching paths and B's own font-index proposal stay complete in their source states. ## 20 — source-convention closure for recurring glyph qualifiers

Source-only printing correction; no image is reopened and no observed reading changes. The supplied `source/SP40_CW_81_witnesses/codex/J81-03/PROMPT.md`, rule 6, lines 99–101, explicitly marks a recurring ambiguous glyph at its first occurrence on each page and prints the later primary unmarked. The current reader brief repeats this convention in its v16/v17 revisions. Root's earlier instructions to add local outer unsure wrappers to five recurring groups are therefore superseded here.

Select C025-E02, C025-S04, C025-S05, C025-S06 and C025-S07 exactly as their complete original C source groups, with no added outer wrappers. The first E01 and S01 groups carry their corresponding first-occurrence qualifiers. Every later occurrence retains its independently observed full candidate states, head/body geometry, index, raised sign, local hand scope and confidence explicitly in the public record and notation. Printed primary and recorded alternative roles remain distinct fields. No path, coordinate, source comment, existing qualifier or other selected glyph is changed by this correction. The five additional wrappers are rescinded before page release; any pending assembler version containing them must retain a bounded source-only before/after record and remove only those added wrapper tokens.

All eight original C outcomes, the R08 two-candidate word, every selected A/B group, the two H-only endpoints and every image-view count remain unchanged. root_count_authorization.literal:
## 16 — final set brace, joined Sigma and open endpoint

Crop: `readers/025/B/12_final_set.png`, full box [735, 886, 1290, 1050], successfully viewed once.

The set's left brace has a long upper upright ending in a leftward cusp, then a separate lower continuation that descends and curls right at its foot. Select complete B025-G08 exactly for that brace, firm, his hand. Keep the following alpha, membership I, tall separator, E_alpha and inclusion outside the brace group. Count one physical C1/H1 for preserved brace geometry, high confidence, kind drawing or diagram, marked_in_H false.

The final Sigma has a faint left curl joining the upper head into the lower descending entry, a clear middle bend, and a flat low foot. The minus is a separate rising horizontal. The index is a clear alpha with an oval loop, an upward right branch, a low right tail and a short internal lower horizontal. A white gap separates the Sigma foot from the alpha. Select complete A025-S08, preserving its additional short alpha-internal path as well as the other four paths. The joined head, alpha and minus are firm, his hand; no recurring detached-head or short-i qualification is transferred here. C's joined-curl group and B's own font-alpha state remain complete in their reader fields. Count one physical C1/H1, high confidence, kind drawing or diagram, marked_in_H false. H's note about the index expected mathematically does not settle an ink reading; retain the observed alpha, with no mathematical correction or proof claim.

The written expression ends at the final alpha tail. No closing brace or added punctuation is visible after it in this endpoint crop; all three complete returns also retain the open endpoint. Keep the final set unclosed. This preserves C's source slip entry separately from the eight original C doubts and differs from H's closing brace. Count C0/H1, high confidence, kind text not on the page, marked_in_H false. The apparent lack of a closing brace is recorded as a manuscript feature and does not authorize supplying one.

## 19 — supplemental endpoint decision and source-agreement closure

This section uses the already once-viewed section 10 crop, `readers/025/A/crops/09_mut_disjoints.png`; it records no additional image display. The terminal t/s strokes of disjoints reach the visible right paper boundary. No separate full stop survives there. The edge supplies no further paper on which to decide a lost or clipped point. Retain disjoints without a final point, preserving C and all three reader texts. Against H's disjoints., count C0/H1, medium confidence, kind text not on the page, marked_in_H false. This is a separate physical endpoint from the raised-t abbreviation and retains the physical-edge limitation explicitly.

The three complete independent readings agree on the remaining ordinary companions and region order: opening live words and inclusion; display equality and limit; quantifier and the pi-zero companions; live les; Il faut voir que, et les, sont, en termes de i et de; the ordinary parenthetical; i.e.; Je dis before the selected que group; final K setminus braced i equality and the set's membership/inclusion companions. Those reader half-read agreements carry no new C/H count. Preserve the selected source's complete surrounding text and every existing path's own coordinate units and placements; root makes no rendered or metric equality claim.

All three independently report archive sheet number 24 at the lower left, with hand undetermined, and all three supply the exact comment `% archive sheet number: 24`. Retain that comment and an explicit archive inventory row under the established conventions. No root image was needed for this agreed item. The region-container rows preserve their actual raw reader hand/scopes; they do not add physical correction counts. Source-only S coverage remains seven distinct source rows with no local scan025 correction assigned and C0/H0; no mathematical verification event is recorded for reading them.

Root physical correction totals authorized by sections 01–19: C25, H27. Twenty-five physical clusters differ from both witnesses; two additional endpoints differ only from H. All eight original C rows remain separate source identities: R07 resolved; R01–R06 and R08 retained. R08 retains two final whole-word candidates after the explicit initial-accent decision. All local H flags are false for the exact reasons and scopes above. Root has successfully viewed 18 distinct existing crops, each once, zero whole scans or supplied halves. The two initially failed image deliveries remain recorded as unseen attempts followed by successful single recovery displays.

S source-only scalar closure: all seven rows have confidence high for the exact source-scope assignment that no local scan025 correction is supplied. This confidence does not assess ink or mathematics. Their C0/H0 counts, lack of local crop and absence of proof events remain unchanged.

Crop: `readers/025/C/14_lower_sigmas.png`, full box [275, 785, 710, 915], successfully viewed once.

The first lower Sigma has a tiny initial dark head piece, a small visible gap, and then a long shallow rising head run. The body starts below that run, curves through the middle and returns to a long rising low foot with a downward right hook. A separate plus is clear. Its index is only a short bent dark stroke, with no separate dot. Select complete C025-S06, preserving the separate tiny head piece and long run, and add one outer unsure wrapper locally. Retain all four complete states in source order: Sigma_i^+ with detached head/retrace; Sigma_prime^+ with detached head/retrace; Sigma_i^+ with independent upper run; Sigma_prime^+ with independent upper run. His hand applies to the body/index/plus, with undetermined hand restricted to the independent-upper-run candidate. A's own continuous head and B's complete own state remain separately sourced. Count C1/H1, medium confidence, kind drawing or diagram, marked_in_H false.

The second lower Sigma has a detached upper run with a paler left entry, a separate body curving through the middle, and a low foot that bends downward at its right end. Its upper minus is a thick separate horizontal. Its index is a single short near-vertical dark stroke, with no separate dot. Select complete C025-S07, adding one outer unsure wrapper locally, and retain the same four whole states with minus in place of plus, in C's original order. His hand applies to the main glyph; undetermined hand remains restricted to the independent-upper-run candidate. Count C1/H1, medium confidence, kind drawing or diagram, marked_in_H false. Preserve every selected C coordinate and path in both groups; the local wrappers are the only changes.

The intervening i.e. has its own dotted i, point, reduced e and final point; keep it ordinary and unexpanded, outside both glyph groups. The separate final sentence point after the second Sigma stays outside that group. Neither lower Sigma is an original C doubt row; both receive new complete local qualification records.

R25-0015.literal:
## 15 — final que and separate adjacent point

Crop: `readers/025/B/15_que_adjacent_point.png`, full box [1040, 788, 1170, 912], successfully viewed once.

The final que has an open q loop, a very long descending stem ending in a short left foot, and joined low u/e strokes ending in a downward right hook. A separate small dark triangular point lies to the right of the upper portion of the descender, with clear white separation from the letters. Select complete B025-G09 exactly, including its literal que, full descender, point and whole-group qualification. The word que remains firm, his hand; only the separate point retains unresolved hand, role, attachment and surface origin. A and C have ordinary que in their complete bounded final-prose frames and no corresponding point group; record those exact source frames, without assigning them an invented negative image finding. Count one physical C1/H1 for the preserved point and its complete source-positioned group, medium confidence, kind drawing or diagram, marked_in_H false; point attribution itself is low confidence. Keep this point distinct from the sentence point after the preceding Sigma. No original C doubt belongs to this locus.

R25-0016.literal:
## 16 — final set brace, joined Sigma and open endpoint

Crop: `readers/025/B/12_final_set.png`, full box [735, 886, 1290, 1050], successfully viewed once.

The set's left brace has a long upper upright ending in a leftward cusp, then a separate lower continuation that descends and curls right at its foot. Select complete B025-G08 exactly for that brace, firm, his hand. Keep the following alpha, membership I, tall separator, E_alpha and inclusion outside the brace group. Count one physical C1/H1 for preserved brace geometry, high confidence, kind drawing or diagram, marked_in_H false.

The final Sigma has a faint left curl joining the upper head into the lower descending entry, a clear middle bend, and a flat low foot. The minus is a separate rising horizontal. The index is a clear alpha with an oval loop, an upward right branch, a low right tail and a short internal lower horizontal. A white gap separates the Sigma foot from the alpha. Select complete A025-S08, preserving its additional short alpha-internal path as well as the other four paths. The joined head, alpha and minus are firm, his hand; no recurring detached-head or short-i qualification is transferred here. C's joined-curl group and B's own font-alpha state remain complete in their reader fields. Count one physical C1/H1, high confidence, kind drawing or diagram, marked_in_H false. H's note about the index expected mathematically does not settle an ink reading; retain the observed alpha, with no mathematical correction or proof claim.

The written expression ends at the final alpha tail. No closing brace or added punctuation is visible after it in this endpoint crop; all three complete returns also retain the open endpoint. Keep the final set unclosed. This preserves C's source slip entry separately from the eight original C doubts and differs from H's closing brace. Count C0/H1, high confidence, kind text not on the page, marked_in_H false. The apparent lack of a closing brace is recorded as a manuscript feature and does not authorize supplying one.

## 17 — faint lower-sheet curve and detached left foot

Crop: `readers/025/B/14_lower_curve.png`, full box [431, 1299, 512, 1372], successfully viewed once.

A faint upper curved run bends rightward and down, then continues through a paler middle section. Below it, a darker slant descends left into a short nearly horizontal foot. A still farther-left short pale foot segment is separated from that low run by a light gap. Select complete B025-M01 with all four components: upper curve, pale middle, lower diagonal/foot and detached left foot. Preserve B's native outer lower-sheet placement as well as the complete child group; the child alone is insufficient to locate the mark. Keep role, hand, attachment and surface origin undetermined, with the local qualification intact. C's own three-component group and A's bounded source frame without a faint-curve group remain accurately reported. Count C1/H1 for this omitted mark cluster, low confidence, kind drawing or diagram, marked_in_H false. H's blank-area description supplies no local doubt mark. No letter, number, mathematical sign or front/back attribution is imposed on these traces.

Select complete B025-M02 exactly and preserve both points, together with B's full native outer lower-sheet placement shared with B025-M01. The current reader brief repeats this convention in its v16/v17 revisions. Root's earlier instructions to add local outer unsure wrappers to five recurring groups are therefore superseded here.

Select C025-E02, C025-S04, C025-S05, C025-S06 and C025-S07 exactly as their complete original C source groups, with no added outer wrappers. The first E01 and S01 groups carry their corresponding first-occurrence qualifiers. Printed primary and recorded alternative roles remain distinct fields. No path, coordinate, source comment, existing qualifier or other selected glyph is changed by this correction. The five additional wrappers are rescinded before page release; any pending assembler version containing them must retain a bounded source-only before/after record and remove only those added wrapper tokens.

All physical counts remain C25/H27: the counts already cover observed geometry and reading scopes, never a wrapper-only change. All eight original C outcomes, the R08 two-candidate word, every selected A/B group, the two H-only endpoints and every image-view count remain unchanged. Preserve sections 08, 09, 12 and 14 as historical root decisions with this explicit printing correction attached. No reader-brief body revision is needed for this point; the existing brief states the correct rule.
